title: Daily Market Digest
subtitle: Market insights as of Friday, October 30, 2026 (based on Oct 29 close and Oct 30 pre-market)

sections.title: Market Pulse: Tech Drag, Inflation Concerns Weigh on Investor Confidence

items.headline: U.S. Markets Close Lower Amid Tech Weakness and Elevated Inflation
items.summary: U.S. stock markets closed lower on Thursday, ending a three-day winning streak, as disappointing earnings and guidance from major AI-powered tech companies significantly dampened investor confidence. An elevated reading of a key inflation gauge further contributed to the negative sentiment, pushing all three major indices into negative territory. Not financial advice.

sections.title: Top Movers: Earnings Drive Significant Swings

items.headline: Workhorse Group Jumps on Strategic Partnership
items.summary: Workhorse Group surged +20% in Friday's trading after announcing a strategic partnership with UK-based AI infrastructure developer Rhaelm Holdings to jointly commercialize its new modular data center platform, TerraPod.

items.headline: CareDx Rises on Strong Q3 Earnings Beat
items.summary: CareDx gained +15% on Friday after reporting third-quarter adjusted EPS of $0.70, significantly beating estimates by $0.44, with revenue climbing 39% year-over-year to $139 million.

items.headline: Intel Plummets on Weak Q4 Guidance
items.summary: Intel shares plunged around 26% in pre-market trading Friday after the chipmaker issued weaker-than-expected fourth-quarter guidance, citing ongoing weakness in the PC market and manufacturing bottlenecks.

items.headline: Amazon Tumbles on Disappointing Q3 and AI Spending Concerns
items.summary: Amazon's stock tumbled around 7% in Friday's pre-market session following its third-quarter earnings report, which disappointed investors and highlighted increasing concerns over its aggressive AI capital expenditures.

items.headline: Defensive Healthcare and Real Estate Sectors Lead While Tech Lags
items.summary: On Thursday, the Health Care Select Sector SPDR ($XLV) rallied 2.4%, and the Real Estate Select Sector SPDR ($XLRE) gained 2.2%, as investors rotated into more defensive areas of the market. Conversely, the Communication Services Select Sector SPDR ($XLC) declined 1.9% and Information Technology fell 1.2%, heavily impacted by the disappointing earnings from tech giants.

items.headline: Federal Reserve Holds Rates Steady, Signals Less Forward Guidance
items.summary: The Federal Reserve held the fed funds target range at 3.75% to 4.00% at its October meeting. Chairman Kevin Warsh indicated a shift towards fewer scheduled rate-setting meetings and reduced forward guidance, encouraging markets to rely more on economic data.

items.headline: Inflation Remains Elevated in September, PCE Index Rises
items.summary: Newly released data shows the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) index rose 0.5% in September, with the annual rate increasing to a four-month high of 3.6%. Core PCE, excluding volatile food and energy prices, increased 0.3% month-over-month and 3.1% year-over-year, indicating persistent inflationary pressures.

items.headline: U.S. Q3 GDP Strong at 3.4% Annual Growth, Boosted by AI Investment
items.summary: The U.S. economy saw a robust 3.4% annual growth in the third quarter, with non-residential fixed investment, particularly in equipment, soaring by 20.9% due to an artificial intelligence-led investment boom. Household spending also contributed with a 3.8% growth.

items.headline: AbbVie and General Dynamics Report Solid Q3 Earnings
items.summary: AbbVie ($ABBV) reported strong third-quarter 2026 results with diluted EPS of $2.37 (GAAP) and adjusted diluted EPS of $3.82, alongside net revenues of $17.404 billion, a 10.3% increase. General Dynamics ($GD) also posted solid third-quarter results, with revenue growing 12.9% to $14.6 billion and diluted EPS increasing 15.7% to $4.49.
